cards.text: Jesus has finished speaking to His disciples. Now He lifts up His eyes to heaven and prays. Friend, lean in, because His first words are "Father, the hour has come."

cards.question: Jesus asks the Father to glorify His Son. What reason does He give?

answers.text: So the Son may glorify the Father
So the crowds will follow the Son
So the disciples will stop worrying

cards.text: Jesus says the Father gave Him authority over all people. ALL people, friend, and I can't even get authority over my own oven timer.

cards.question: With authority over all people, what does Jesus give to all those the Father has given Him?

cards.text: Now, if you asked me what eternal life means, I'd say a cookie box that never runs empty. Jesus defines it a whole lot better than that.

cards.question: So what does Jesus say eternal life is?

answers.text: Knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ
Keeping every law without one slip

cards.text: Then Jesus tells the Father He has already glorified Him on earth. Not someday, friend. ALREADY.

cards.question: How does Jesus say He glorified the Father on earth?

answers.text: By accomplishing the work the Father gave Him
By gathering a great army for the Father
By building a new temple for the Father

cards.text: And now Jesus asks the Father for glory again. This time, it's glory in the Father's presence.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus asks for the glory He had with the Father before the world existed.

cards.text: Now the prayer turns to the disciples. Jesus says He revealed the Father's name to the ones the Father gave Him out of the world.

cards.question: Jesus says the disciples were the Father's, and the Father gave them to Him. What does He say they've done with the Father's word?

cards.text: They know now that everything the Father gave Jesus comes from the Father. Jesus gave them the Father's words, and they received them, no returns and no exchanges.

cards.question: The disciples received the words Jesus gave them. What did they know with certainty?

answers.text: That Jesus came from the Father
That they would never be scattered
That Jesus would be crowned king soon

cards.text: Jesus is still praying, and now He says exactly who He's asking for. It's the ones the Father gave Him, because they belong to the Father.

cards.question: Jesus is asking on behalf of those the Father gave Him. Who does He say He is NOT asking on behalf of here?

cards.text: Jesus says everything He has belongs to the Father, and everything the Father has belongs to Him. Then He says He won't be in the world anymore, but the disciples still are.

cards.question: Jesus asks the Holy Father to protect the disciples by His name. What for?

answers.text: So they may rule the nations

cards.text: Jesus says that while He was with them, He protected and preserved them by the Father's name. It's like me counting my six cookie cutters on the counter every night, keeping track of every one.

cards.question: Jesus says, "Not one of them has been ___, except the son of destruction"
True or false: Jesus says the son of destruction was lost so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.

cards.text: Now Jesus is coming to the Father. And He's saying all this out loud while He's still in the world.

cards.question: Why does Jesus say these things while He's still in the world?

answers.text: So His joy may be fulfilled in them
So the crowds can hear Him pray
So the priests cannot accuse Him

cards.text: Jesus has given the disciples the Father's word. Then He tells the Father what that word has gotten them from the world.

cards.question: How has the world treated the disciples?

cards.text: Jesus says they aren't of the world, just as He isn't of the world. Me? After years in a junk drawer, friend, I'd be begging for the EXIT.

cards.question: Jesus doesn't ask the Father to take the disciples out of the world. What does He ask instead?

answers.text: That the Father keep them from the evil one
That the Father make them powerful in it
That the Father hide them away for a while

cards.text: Jesus says it again: they aren't of the world, just as He isn't. Then He asks the Father to sanctify them by the truth.

cards.question: Jesus prays, "Sanctify them by the truth; Your ___ is truth."
Jesus says the Father sent Him into the world. True or false: Jesus says He has sent the disciples into the world too.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, "For them I sanctify Myself, so that they too may be sanctified by the truth." For them, friend, every bit of it.
Then the prayer gets WIDER. Jesus says He isn't asking on behalf of the disciples alone.

cards.question: Who else does Jesus pray for?

answers.text: Those who will believe through their message
The priests serving in the temple

cards.text: That's right, friend, which means Jesus prayed for every baker who believes, and for one dusty stamper from a junk drawer. He prays they'd all be one, as the Father is in Him and He is in the Father.

cards.question: Jesus prays that all believers may be one and be in the Father and the Son. Why?

answers.text: So the world may believe the Father sent Him
So they can outnumber all their enemies
So they will never have to disagree

cards.text: Jesus says He has given them the glory the Father gave Him, so they may be one as the Father and the Son are one. One glory, one family, ONE.

cards.question: Jesus prays they'd be perfectly united, so the world may know the Father sent Him. What else will the world know?

answers.text: That the Father loves them as He loves Jesus
That they are better than everyone else
That all their troubles are finally over

cards.text: Then Jesus tells the Father what He wants for those the Father has given Him. Friend, this one gets me right in the apron.

cards.question: What does Jesus want for those the Father has given Him?

answers.text: To be with Him where He is
To rule over all the nations
To go back home to Galilee

cards.question: Jesus wants them to see the glory the Father gave Him. True or false: Jesus says the Father started loving Him when He came into the world.

cards.text: Jesus prays, "Righteous Father, although the world has not known You, I know You, and they know that You sent Me."

cards.question: Jesus says He has made the Father's ___ known to them, and He'll keep making it known.
Why does Jesus keep making the Father's name known to them?

answers.text: So the Father's love for Him may be in them
So the whole world will fear the Father
So the disciples can win every argument

cards.text: And that's where Jesus ends His prayer: the Father's love in them, and Jesus in them. Friend, I spent years in the dark thinking I was forgotten, and here's Jesus praying for His Father's love to be in His people.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 6 quotes "Not one of them has been ___, except the son of destruction", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 15 quotes "Sanctify them by the truth; Your ___ is truth.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1 has 7 choice cards, and 6 of them are multiple choice (cards 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 14). There is one true or false (card 10) and no fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Stop 3 has 7 choice cards, and 5 of them are multiple choice (cards 2, 4, 6, 8 and 12). There is one true or false (card 9) and one fill in the blank (card 11). Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus tells the Father 'what that word has gotten them from the world,' which makes the Father's word the cause of the world's hatred. John 17:14 only puts the two side by side ('I have given them Your word and the world has hated them'). The reason the verse does give is 'For they are not of the world.' The card adds a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The comparison makes up a new backstory habit: Papa Dorin counting his six cookie cutters on the Millers' counter every night. That is the Millers' kitchen, not his bakery, so it adds to his backstory. It is also an awkward fit, because the backstory says all six cutters were taken from him, while the verse is about none being lost.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The question 'Who else does Jesus pray for?' depends on the earlier story card for what 'else' means. The right answer says 'their message' but never says whose message, and the disciples are not named on this card. That points back to a card the baker can no longer see.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'The son of destruction' first appears on card 6 and is asked about again on card 7, but no card says who he is. John 17:12 does not name him. The surrounding chapters (for example, John 13:26-30) point to Judas Iscariot.
findings.question: Two rules pull in different directions here. The New people rule says to say who someone is the first time they show up. The Leave open rule says to leave open what the text leaves open. Should Papa Dorin identify the son of destruction as Judas Iscariot, citing a verse outside the passage such as John 13:26-30? Or should he leave the name unstated, as with the sons of God in Genesis 6, and rely on a dictionary pop-up?
